correctness.rationale: Three exact polynomial generator identities have positive coefficients of the least generator for all odd n>=7, giving strictly descending reductions to a finite two-rectangle index set. That set has n^2 indices, and gcd(n^2,(n+2)^2)=1 ensures residue-surjectivity, hence unique exact Apéry representatives. Its only maximal coordinatewise corners give both pseudo-Frobenius numbers. Direct algebra yields their cubic formulas and the genus from exact coordinate sums, with a sign check at the switching n=13. The standalone verifier independently computes shortest paths on all residues and checks PF/genus/F in 52 odd cases through n=251; finite checks are not substituted for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Directly inspected close primary sources treat squares of three ordinary consecutive bases, four ordinary consecutive squares, or infinitely many quadratic-sequence terms starting at zero. The finite triple with base spacing two and its exact Apéry/PF/genus formulas are neither their stated cases nor a special-case implication; generic numerical-semigroup algorithms are not a pre-existing exact family classification. Targeted literal, equivalent-formulation, parameter and exact-value searches and historical-claim comparison revealed no covering statement. This supports best-knowledge originality while leaving unindexed earlier derivations as a residual risk.
residual_risks: An inaccessible or unindexed historic result may independently have derived the exact odd-square three-generator Apéry diagram or equivalent numerical invariants.

Generic three-generator algorithms could yield the same formulas with further derivation, so novelty is the explicit parameter-uniform classification, not an algorithm for a single numerical semigroup.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite family generated by three successive odd squares, a canonical arithmetic subsequence of quadratic values distinct from the well-studied consecutive integer-square family. The exact Apéry normal form, complete two-element pseudo-Frobenius set, polynomial genus and sharp Frobenius branch transition are structural invariants that inform singularity/ring structure and enumeration beyond a one-off integer calculation. The result is neither a trivial numeric special case nor an artificial parameter slice.
